issues.issue: Was there a new fact justifying a revision of the Division’s earlier estimate of the length of detention, given the August 2008 preliminary PRRA opinion?
issues.applicant_position: The preliminary PRRA opinion was not a new fact; the Division should not have revised its time estimate.
issues.respondent_position: The preliminary PRRA opinion served August 11, 2008 was a new fact justifying a revised estimate.
issues.result_quote: I do not think that it was appropriate for the Division, at the September 11, 2008 review hearing, to ground an assessment

issues.issue: Was the Division’s estimate of anticipated future length of detention speculative, unreasonable or an error of law?
issues.applicant_position: The Division’s future-detention estimate was premature, speculative and perverse; the Federal Court should have said so.
issues.result_quote: it was a reviewable error of law as well as unreasonable for the Division to speculate on the Minister’s forthcoming decision

issues.issue: Did the Division properly depart from its earlier finding that electronic monitoring would not reduce flight risk adequately?
issues.applicant_position: Electronic monitoring is inefficient to secure removal; the Division gave no clear and compelling reason to depart from its prior finding.
issues.result_quote: There is thus no need to address the issue of the efficiency of the alternatives proposed by the Division to allow the appeal and set aside the release order.

issues.issue: Should the Division have expedited the proceedings as a less drastic way to prevent a s.7 Charter breach, instead of ordering release?
issues.result_quote: the Division failed to take into account and assess relevant factors as well as the impact of another appropriate available and less drastic recourse

issues.issue: Certified question: does lengthy detention become indefinite, and a s.7 breach, when the estimate rests on anticipated pursuit of all IRPA and Federal Court processes?
issues.applicant_position: Federal Court failed to consider whether detention became indefinite, contrary to s.7 of the Charter.
issues.result_quote: the basis of the estimation of anticipated future length detention should be the proceedings as they exist at the time of each monthly review
